name: Dreyer 2023 large MI database

name: Kaya 2018 large MI dataset

name: Jeong 2020 11 upper-limb tasks

name: WBCIC-SHU multi-day MI (Yang 2025)
notes: Trials computed as 51x3x200 (2-class) + 11x3x300 (3-class) from MOABB's description, though Figshare says 52 two-class subjects; MOABB: Yang2025

name: Iwama 2023 high-density SMR-BCI
notes: 128-ch EGI recordings of right-hand MI neurofeedback in 16 blocks over 2 days, with trials as MOABB Total_trials counting rest and MI epochs; MOABB: Iwama2023

name: Yi 2014 simple and compound limb MI
notes: Seven simple and compound limb MI tasks plus rest; MOABB: Weibo2014

name: Leeuwis 2021 MI with psychological factors
notes: Left/right hand MI by BCI-naive students with psychological and cognitive questionnaires; MOABB: Leeuwis2021

name: Liu 2024 acute stroke MI
notes: Left/right hand grasp MI by acute stroke patients, trials computed as 50 x 40 while MOABB loads 47 subjects (1880 trials); MOABB: Liu2024

name: Zuo 2025 lower-limb MI (knee pain)
notes: Left vs right leg MI by knee-pain patients over 5 sessions; MOABB: Zuo2025

name: Shin 2017 hybrid EEG-NIRS MI
notes: Left/right hand MI with simultaneous NIRS, recorded at 1000 Hz and released at 200 Hz; license per MOABB; MOABB: Shin2017A

name: NETBCI longitudinal MI (Corsi 2026)
notes: Right-hand MI vs rest cursor training over 4 days with simultaneous MEG, released at 250 Hz; MOABB: NETBCI2026

name: Wang 2026 sensory-guided MI training
notes: MI-BCI training study with 4 groups over 5 sessions, shipped as trial-segmented MATLAB files; MOABB: Wang2026

name: WAY-EEG-GAL (Kaggle Grasp-and-Lift)
notes: Grasp-and-lift with varying weight and friction, also the basis of Kaggle's Grasp-and-Lift EEG Detection competition (registration, competition rules); not in MOABB

name: BCI Challenge @ NER 2015 (Kaggle)

name: BCI Competition II IIb (Wadsworth P300)
notes: 6x6 P300 speller recorded in 3 sessions; not in MOABB

name: BCI Competition III II (Wadsworth P300)
notes: 6x6 P300 speller, trials computed as character epochs 2 x (85 train + 100 test); not in MOABB

name: Riccio 2013 ALS P300 speller
notes: P300 speller used by people with ALS, about 3500 non-target and 700 target epochs per subject per MOABB; MOABB: BNCI2014_008

name: Arico 2014 P300 speller
notes: Grid and geo-speller P300 paradigms over 3 sessions (MOABB loads the grid speller); MOABB: BNCI2014_009

name: AMUSE auditory spatial ERP
notes: Auditory BCI with six spatial speakers; MOABB: BNCI2015_009

name: Brain Invaders 2013a
notes: P300 videogame in adaptive and non-adaptive modes, with subjects 1-7 recorded in 8 sessions; MOABB: BI2013a

name: Brain Invaders 2014a
notes: Calibration-less P300 videogame with dry electrodes (64 of 71 recruited released); MOABB: BI2014a

name: Brain Invaders 2015a
notes: P300 videogame with three flash durations; MOABB: BI2015a

name: Brain Invaders 2015b (multi-user)
notes: Pairs playing a cooperative or competitive P300 videogame; MOABB: BI2015b

name: OpenBMI (Lee 2019) ERP
notes: 6x6 row-column face speller over 2 sessions, about 6900 non-target and 1380 target epochs per subject per MOABB; MOABB: Lee2019_ERP

name: Hübner 2017 label-proportion speller
notes: Visual matrix speller with unsupervised learning from label proportions, sentence spelled 3 times; MOABB: Huebner2017

name: Sosulski 2019 auditory oddball SOA
notes: Auditory oddball under varying stimulus onset asynchronies in many short runs; MOABB: Sosulski2019

name: EPFL P300 (Hoffmann 2008)
notes: Six-image P300 paradigm with disabled and able-bodied users over 4 sessions, license unknown per MOABB; MOABB: EPFLP300

name: Mobile BCI ERP (Lee 2021)
notes: ERP paradigm of the Mobile BCI dataset (up to 5 sessions), channels left blank because MOABB lists both 32 and 48 EEG channels; MOABB: Lee2021Mobile_ERP

name: bigP3BCI (Mainsah 2025)
notes: approx: subjects summed over 20 P300-speller studies (participants may overlap; 47 target end users), with 16 or 32 channels by study per MOABB; MOABB: Mainsah2025_A to Mainsah2025_S2

name: Won 2022 RSVP and P300 speller
notes: Resting state, RSVP (40 trials) and P300 speller (2 calibration + 4 test runs) per participant; not in MOABB

name: Tsinghua RSVP benchmark (Zhang 2020)
notes: RSVP target detection with 1024000 image presentations, recorded at 1000 Hz and released at 250 Hz; not in MOABB

name: Tsinghua SSVEP benchmark (Wang 2016)
notes: 40-target speller, trials computed as 6 blocks x 40, license per MOABB which loads a Zenodo mirror; MOABB: Wang2016

name: BETA SSVEP benchmark
notes: 40-target speller recorded outside a shielded room, trials computed as 4 blocks x 40, license per MOABB; MOABB: Liu2020BETA

name: eldBETA SSVEP (elderly)
notes: Participants aged 51-81 on a 9-target speller, trials computed as 7 blocks x 9, also on the Tsinghua site; MOABB: Liu2022EldBETA

name: OpenBMI (Lee 2019) SSVEP
notes: 4-target SSVEP, trials computed as 54 x 2 sessions x 200 (offline and online phases); MOABB: Lee2019_SSVEP

name: Nakanishi 2015 12-class SSVEP
notes: 12-target JFPM SSVEP, trials computed as 12 targets x 15, license unknown per MOABB; MOABB: Nakanishi2015

name: MAMEM SSVEP dataset 1
notes: Five-frequency SSVEP with a 256-channel EGI net, with companion sets MAMEM2 and MAMEM3; MOABB: MAMEM1

name: Dong 2023 adolescent SSVEP
notes: 40-target JFPM SSVEP by ages 10-16 at the BCI Olympics with semi-dry electrodes, trials computed as 4 blocks x 40; MOABB: Dong2023

name: Kim 2025 beta-range 40-class SSVEP
notes: 40-target speller with 14-21.8 Hz stimulation for lower fatigue, trials computed as 6 blocks x 40; MOABB: Kim2025BetaRange

name: Wearable SSVEP dataset (Zhu 2021)
notes: 12-target wireless headband with dry and wet electrodes, trials computed as 102 x 240; not in MOABB

name: Thielen 2015 broad-band VEP
notes: 36-class Gold-code speller with reconvolution modelling; MOABB: Thielen2015

name: Thielen 2021 zero-training c-VEP
notes: 20-class Gold-code speller with 8 electrodes, trials computed as 5 blocks x 20; MOABB: Thielen2021

name: Castillos 2023 burst c-VEP
notes: Burst vs m-sequence codes at 40% and 100% amplitude, trials computed as 4 conditions x 15 blocks x 4, MOABB lists 28 channels; MOABB: CastillosCVEP100 (plus CastillosCVEP40, CastillosBurstVEP40, CastillosBurstVEP100)

name: Martínez-Cagigal 2023 p-ary c-VEP
notes: 16-command speller comparing five p-ary m-sequence conditions (base 2 to 11), with a companion checkerboard dataset; MOABB: MartinezCagigal2023Pary

name: Zheng 2024 narrow-band c-VEP
notes: 40-target narrow-band random-sequence c-VEP (2 paradigms) plus one JFPM SSVEP paradigm, trials computed as 9 blocks x 40; not in MOABB

name: TUH EEG Corpus (TUEG)
notes: v2.0.2 holds 26,846 clinical sessions in 70,831 EDF files sampled at 250-1024 Hz in over 40 channel configurations; free, but needs a signed request form emailed to NEDC.

name: Harvard Electroencephalography Database (HEEDB)
notes: Version 4.1 has 284,343 routine, EMU and ICU EEG studies from four Harvard hospitals with linked reports and no stated hour total; the AWS registry entry names the BDSP Restricted Health Data License instead.

name: Healthy Brain Network EEG (HBN-EEG)
notes: Subjects summed over releases R1-R11 (ds005505-ds005516) of children and young adults (5-21 y) doing resting state plus several tasks; an extra non-commercial release is under CC-BY-NC-SA.

name: TUH Abnormal EEG Corpus (TUAB)
notes: v3.0.1 has 2,993 EDF files (one per session) labelled normal or abnormal with a fixed train/eval split; 2,329 unique subjects (2,383 if counted per class, since 54 training subjects appear in both).

name: TUH EEG Seizure Corpus (TUSZ)
notes: approx: hours are the sum of the train/dev/eval durations in the v2.0.6 README, covering 8,140 EDF files in 1,643 sessions with 2,664 annotated seizures.

name: TUH EEG Events Corpus (TUEV)
notes: v2.0.1 has 518 EDF files (359 train, 159 eval) annotated with six classes: spike/sharp wave, GPED, PLED, eye movement, artifact and background; subjects and hours are not stated.

name: TUH EEG Artifact Corpus (TUAR)
notes: v3.0.1 has 310 EDF files in 259 sessions with 160,073 labelled artifact events (muscle, eye movement, electrode, chewing, shivering and combinations).

name: TUH EEG Epilepsy Corpus (TUEP)
notes: v3.1.0 has 100 patients with epilepsy and 100 without, in 2,808 EDF files across 698 sessions.

name: TUH EEG Slowing Corpus (TUSL)
notes: v2.0.1 has 300 files in 75 sessions with 10 s annotations of slowing, seizure and complex background; recording hours are not stated.

name: CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database
notes: approx: 961.6 h summed from the chb01-chb23 summary files plus 22 chb24 files of about 1 h each, for 664 EDF files in 23 pediatric cases with 198 seizures.

name: Siena Scalp EEG Database
notes: Hours sum subject_info.csv recording minutes (the page says about 128 h, EDF headers sum to 141 h) for 41 EDF files with 47 seizures; one patient has 20 EEG channels.

name: Bonn University EEG (sets A-E)
notes: approx: five sets of 100 single-channel segments of 4,096 samples at 173.61 Hz (about 23.6 s each), so hours are derived.

name: Helsinki neonatal EEG seizure dataset
notes: NICU recordings of 79 term neonates (median 74 min each) with seizures annotated by three experts; 39 neonates had seizures by consensus.

name: HMS Harmful Brain Activity Classification
notes: Trials are expert-voted 50 s EEG segments labelled seizure, LPD, GPD, LRDA, GRDA or other, with counts taken from a paper describing the Kaggle training set; download needs a Kaggle account and accepting the competition rules.

name: I-CARE (post-cardiac-arrest coma EEG)
notes: Continuous ICU EEG from seven hospitals in 80,809 segments with neurological outcome labels (up to 22 EEG channels, availability varies); 413 further patients are held back as hidden test data.

name: SeizeIT2 wearable epilepsy dataset
notes: approx: behind-the-ear EEG plus ECG, EMG and motion from five European epilepsy monitoring units, with 886 focal seizures (README says around 11,640 h, the paper more than 11,000 h).

name: NMT Scalp EEG Dataset
notes: approx: 2,417 clinical recordings from unique patients in Pakistan labelled normal or abnormal (paper says almost 625 h); the NUST download page refused connections when checked, so the access mode is from the paper.

name: CAUEEG
notes: 1,379 clinical EEGs from 1,155 patients at Chung-Ang University Hospital labelled normal, MCI or dementia; access needs an online application and local ethics approval.

name: Alzheimer's, FTD and healthy resting EEG (ds004504)
notes: approx: eyes-closed clinical EEG from 36 Alzheimer's, 23 frontotemporal dementia and 29 control participants, 1,164 min in total per the README.

name: UC San Diego Parkinson's resting EEG (ds002778)
notes: BioSemi rest recordings (about 3 min) of Parkinson's patients on and off medication plus controls; the channel count is the BIDS sidecar's EEGChannelCount, and the authors ask to be emailed before publication.

name: Iowa Parkinson's eyes-open rest (ds004584)
notes: Two minutes of eyes-open rest from 100 Parkinson's patients and 49 controls on a 64-channel BrainVision cap.

name: Parkinson's 3-stim oddball and rest (ds003490)
notes: Rest plus auditory oddball from 25 Parkinson's patients (separate ON and OFF medication sessions) and 25 matched controls.

name: Depression rest (ds003478)
notes: Eyes-open and eyes-closed rest from college-age participants scoring reliably high or low on the Beck Depression Inventory, some clinically interviewed.

name: MODMA (multi-modal mental-disorder dataset)
notes: 128-channel resting and dot-probe EEG from depressed patients and controls, plus 3-electrode resting EEG from 55 people; download needs a signed end-user licence (also on UK Data Service ReShare).

name: MDD patients and healthy controls EEG (Mumtaz)
notes: 34 MDD patients and 30 controls with eyes-closed, eyes-open and P300 task files (193 EDFs); channel count and rate are from the CBraMod paper, not the Figshare page.

name: EEG in schizophrenia (RepOD)
notes: approx: 15 min of eyes-closed rest from each of 14 paranoid schizophrenia patients and 14 controls (28 EDF files), so hours are derived.

name: First-episode psychosis rest (ds003944)
notes: Five minutes of eyes-open rest from first-episode psychosis patients and controls, recorded with a 60-channel cap on an Elekta MEG system (sample 1 of 2).

name: EEG data for ADHD/control children
notes: 61 children with ADHD and 60 controls aged 7-12 during a visual attention (counting) task; files need a free IEEE account.

name: TDBRAIN
notes: 1,346 resting-state sessions (eyes open and closed) from psychiatric patients, mainly MDD and ADHD, collected 2001-2021; needs ORCID login and a signed DUA.

name: Sleep-EDF Expanded
notes: 197 whole-night PSGs (153 Sleep Cassette from 78 subjects, 44 Sleep Telemetry from 22 subjects) with Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz EEG; hours summed from EDF headers.

name: Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS)
notes: Home PSGs for 5,793 participants at visit 1 and 2,651 at visit 2 (C3-A2 and C4-A1 EEG); NSRR reviews each data request.

name: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis sleep (MESA)
notes: Raw PSGs for 2,056 of the 2,237 MESA Sleep exam participants (2010-2012), with Fz-Cz, Cz-Oz and C4-M1 EEG.

name: Osteoporotic Fractures in Men sleep (MrOS)
notes: Raw PSGs for 2,907 men at sleep visit 1 and 1,026 at visit 2, aged 65 and older (C3, C4, A1, A2 recorded).

name: Cleveland Family Study (CFS)
notes: Visit 5 in-lab PSGs for 735 members of a 2,284-person family sleep apnea cohort (C3, C4, A1, A2 recorded); non-commercial use only.

name: Childhood Adenotonsillectomy Trial (CHAT)
notes: Baseline and 7-month PSGs for 464 randomized children aged 5-9.9 with mild to moderate OSA, from 1,447 screening PSGs.

name: NCH Sleep DataBank (NCHSDB)
notes: 3,984 pediatric clinical PSGs (2017-2019) from Nationwide Children's Hospital with linked EHR data; non-commercial use only.

name: Wisconsin Sleep Cohort (WSC)
notes: Cohort of 1,500 recruited adults with repeated in-lab PSG about every four years from 1988 to 2015; NSRR file counts are not stated and a separate WSC committee reviews requests (up to three weeks).

name: Haaglanden Medisch Centrum sleep staging (HMC)
notes: 151 clinical whole-night PSGs from a Dutch sleep center (F4-M1, C4-M1, O2-M1, C3-M2); hours summed from EDF headers.

name: ISRUC-Sleep
notes: 126 PSGs in three subgroups (100 patients once, 8 subjects twice, 10 healthy once) scored by two experts, served from MEGA folders; channels and rate are from the CBraMod paper, not the site.

name: Dreem Open Dataset - Healthy (DOD-H)
notes: Clinical PSGs of healthy adult volunteers, each scored by five sleep technologists.

name: Dreem Open Dataset - Obstructive (DOD-O)
notes: PSGs of patients with obstructive sleep apnea scored by five technologists; Zenodo has 56 records, one without a consensus hypnogram.

name: CAP Sleep Database
notes: 108 PSGs (16 healthy, 92 with NFLE, RBD, PLM, insomnia, narcolepsy, SDB or bruxism) with cyclic alternating pattern annotations and at least 3 EEG channels.

name: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2018 (You Snooze You Win)
notes: Hours summed from record headers (7,663.9 training, 7,597.3 test) for PSGs with arousal labels on 994 training subjects and 989 unlabelled test subjects; the page's 1,985 total differs from the 1,983 split counts.

name: Montreal Archive of Sleep Studies (MASS)
notes: 200 lab PSG nights (cohort C1, subsets SS1-SS5); biosignals need ethics approval, a project description and acceptance of a licence, with only annotations downloadable directly.

name: Human Sleep Project (HSP)
notes: Version 3.0 has 115,129 clinical PSGs plus 4,105 home sleep apnea tests from five US academic centers; native sampling rates vary and hours are not stated.

name: Bitbrain Open Access Sleep (BOAS)
notes: 128 nights recorded simultaneously with clinical PSG (F3, F4, C3, C4, O1, O2) and a 2-channel forehead EEG headband.

name: MPI Leipzig Mind-Brain-Body (LEMON)
notes: approx: 16 min of interleaved eyes-closed and eyes-open rest per healthy young or elderly adult, so hours are derived; preprocessed data cover 203 participants.

name: Cuban Human Brain Mapping Project (CHBMP)
notes: Population-based normative EEG of at least 30 min (eyes closed, eyes open, hyperventilation, recovery) with 64 channels for 170 participants and 120 for 80; Synapse login required.

name: SRM resting-state EEG (ds003775)
notes: Four minutes of eyes-closed rest per healthy adult (BioSemi 64), with a retest session for a subset.

name: Dortmund Vital Study resting EEG (ds005385)
notes: Healthy adults aged 20-70 with 3 min eyes open and closed before and after a 2-hour cognitive block, plus a 5-year follow-up session.

name: Test-retest resting and cognitive state EEG (ds004148)
notes: Eyes-closed and eyes-open rest plus three cognitive tasks repeated over three sessions.

name: DEAP
notes: approx: hours = 40 one-minute music videos x 32 people; signed EULA from permanent academic staff only, preprocessed copy at 128 Hz, live site returned 503 on 2026-11-03 so figures come from the archived readme.

name: SEED
notes: approx: hours assume ~4-min clips x 15 clips x 3 sessions; access needs a signed license agreement uploaded to the BCMI apply form, and preprocessed EEG is at 200 Hz.

name: SEED-IV
notes: Four emotions over 3 sessions x 24 trials; page gives only the 200 Hz downsampled rate, and access is via the BCMI license agreement and application.

name: SEED-V
notes: Five emotions over 3 sessions x 15 clips with eye movements; page gives only the 200 Hz downsampled rate.

name: SEED-VII
notes: approx: hours = 20 subjects x the stated ~14,098 s of video; six basic emotions plus neutral with continuous labels over 4 sessions.

name: SEED-SD
notes: Emotion under sleep deprivation, recovery and normal sleep, 24 clips per session, with eye tracking.

name: SEED-GER
notes: German participants for cross-cultural emotion recognition; page says 20 clips but 21 trials per session, so trials are left blank.

name: SEED-FRA
notes: French participants for cross-cultural emotion recognition, 21 clips x 3 sessions, with eye movements.

name: DREAMER
notes: Emotiv EPOC and ECG during 18 film clips; Zenodo files are restricted behind an access-request form, and clip, channel and rate figures come from TorchEEG docs because the paper was not readable.

name: AMIGOS
notes: Emotiv EPOC during 16 short videos (40 people) plus 4 long videos (37 people, some in groups); access needs a signed EULA from an institutional email.

name: MAHNOB-HCI
notes: 30 recorded and 27 usable participants watching 20 emotional videos; the account-request portal returned 404 on 2026-11-03, and the paper gives 1024 Hz downsampled to 256 Hz only for peripheral signals.

name: FACED
notes: Nine emotion categories from 28 clips; recorded at 250 or 1000 Hz depending on cohort, and Synapse needs a free account to download.

name: EAV
notes: approx: hours = 8,400 interactions x 20 s; EEG, audio and video in a cue-based conversation with 5 emotions, Zenodo access is restricted under a data usage agreement.

name: Imagined Emotion (ds003004)
notes: Guided imagination of 15 emotions; channel count and rate are from the BIDS sidecar of sub-01.

name: THINGS-EEG2
notes: RSVP of 16,740 THINGS image conditions with 82,160 trials per participant; the standard benchmark for EEG image decoding and reconstruction.

name: THINGS-EEG1
notes: approx: about 1 h per subject of 10 Hz RSVP over 22,248 images from 1,854 concepts; paper says 64 electrodes while the BIDS sidecar lists 63 EEG channels (reference Cz).

name: Alljoined1
notes: NSD natural images built for EEG-to-image decoding; the HF split holds 43,070 epochs against 46,080 in the abstract, and no license tag is set.

name: Alljoined-1.6M
notes: approx: trials = 20 x 83,520 and hours = ~8 h per subject; consumer Emotiv Flex 2 on the THINGS-EEG2 image set, with a non-commercial terms prompt on the card though the repo is not gated.

name: EEG-ImageNet
notes: 4,000 ImageNet-21k images in 80 classes with multi-granularity labels; README links a direct cloud download, while the 2025 v2 preprint (renamed CrossPT-EEG) says access is after review.

name: Spampinato EEG-ImageNet (PeRCeiVe)
notes: 40 ImageNet classes x 50 images shown in class blocks; the block design is known to confound class with recording time, so treat decoding results with care.

name: SEED-DV
notes: EEG to video decoding (EEG2Video) with 1,400 clips over 40 concepts per subject; access needs the BCMI license and application forms.

name: Object Category EEG Dataset (OCED)
notes: 72 object photos in 6 categories each shown 72 times per participant on a 128-channel EGI net; the paper analysed 124 electrodes.

name: Wakeman-Henson faces (ds002718)
notes: EEG-only EEGLAB release of the famous/unfamiliar/scrambled face task; the full MEG+EEG original is ds000117 and this copy is downsampled to 250 Hz.

name: Go/no-go categorization (ds002680)
notes: Rapid animal/non-animal go/no-go categorization of natural scenes over 2 sessions; the 31 channels are labelled misc in the BIDS sidecar.

name: KU Leuven AAD
notes: Two competing Dutch stories with about 72 min per subject; shared data are at 128 Hz, and the authors warn about trial-fingerprint and gaze-bias leakage in decoders.

name: DTU AAD
notes: Two-talker selective attention in ~50 s trials across 3 reverberation conditions, plus single-talker trials, with audio included.

name: DTU hearing-impaired AAD
notes: 22 hearing-impaired and 22 normal-hearing listeners in BIDS with two-talker attention, ERPs, EFRs and resting state; channel count and rate were not on the record page.

name: AV-GC-AAD
notes: approx: hours = 8 ten-minute trials per subject; gaze-controlled AAD built to expose eye-gaze shortcuts, with 3 of 16 subjects not shared.

name: SparrKULee
notes: 90-150 min of Dutch speech per participant, provided at 1024 Hz; 196 of 4,338 files are restricted and need an email request.

name: Natural speech (Broderick/Di Liberto, ds004408)
notes: approx: trials assume 20 runs per subject as in sub-001; audiobook listening (The Old Man and the Sea) in runs of ~3 min with word and phoneme TextGrids; the wider Dryad bundle adds cocktail-party, reversed-speech and N400 sets.

name: Kara One
notes: approx: about 132 trials per participant of imagined and spoken phonemes/words with face and audio; the page reports 62 EEG channels but no sampling rate.

name: Inner Speech (Nieto)
notes: approx: more than 9 h in total; Spanish words up/down/left/right as inner, pronounced and visualized speech, plus 8 EOG/EMG channels.

name: BCI Competition 2020 Track 3 imagined speech
notes: approx: 350 train/validation trials per subject plus 50 test trials released separately; five words or phrases.

name: FEIS
notes: Emotiv EPOC+ during heard, imagined and spoken English phonemes (16), plus 2 Mandarin-speaking participants; the record states free academic non-profit use.

name: Chisco
notes: approx: over 20,000 sentence trials and more than 900 min per subject in the paper's 3 subjects; OpenNeuro now holds 5 subjects of Chinese imagined-sentence EEG.

name: NMED-T
notes: Dense-array EEG during 10 full-length songs at varied tempi with tapping data; preprocessed release is at 125 Hz.

name: OpenMIIR
notes: Music perception and imagery of 12 short fragments; channel and rate figures come from a follow-up paper by the same authors.

name: MUSIN-G (ds003774)
notes: Indian participants listening to 12 songs of different genres with familiarity and enjoyment ratings.

name: ZuCo 1.0
notes: approx: 4-6 h of natural sentence reading per subject with simultaneous eye tracking, covering 21,629 words.

name: ZuCo 2.0
notes: 739 sentences in normal and task-specific reading with eye tracking; sessions lasted 100-180 min.

name: Alice EEG (Brennan)
notes: Passive listening to a 12-min Alice chapter; the paper recorded 52 people (3 lost to error) and the Deep Blue page was behind a bot check, so the license is unverified.

name: ChineseEEG
notes: approx: about 13 h of silent novel reading per participant per the paper, while the OpenNeuro README says about 11 h.

name: TMNRED
notes: approx: over 10 h of Chinese natural sentence reading for fuzzy semantic target detection; the paper gives 400-450 trials per subject yet over 4,000 in total.

name: DERCo
notes: Narrative reading EEG paired with cloze next-word predictability from 500 online participants.

name: ERP CORE
notes: Six optimized paradigms for N170, MMN, N2pc, N400, P3, LRP and ERN with full pipelines.

name: COG-BCI
notes: approx: over 100 h of EEG and ECG across 3 sessions of N-back, MATB-II, PVT and flanker tasks for passive BCI.

name: STEW

name: EEGMAT (mental arithmetic)
notes: Rest versus serial-subtraction EEG on a Neurocom 23-channel system with good and bad counter groups; channel count and rate were not stated on the page.

name: Shin 2018 n-back/DSR/WG (EEG-NIRS)
notes: Simultaneous EEG and NIRS during n-back, discrimination/selection response and word generation tasks.

name: SEED-VIG
notes: approx: about 2 h of simulated driving per subject with PERCLOS vigilance labels; 12 posterior + 6 temporal EEG channels plus forehead EOG.
